walkthroughs.body_html:
Analysing the Strategic Position of a Business — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Analysing the Strategic Position of a Business brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Analysing the Strategic Position of a Business.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Porter's three generic strategies are cost leadership, differentiation and:
options: Diversification
Focus
Innovation
Acquisition

mcqs.q: The 'Blue Ocean' concept was proposed by:
options: Porter
Kim and Mauborgne
Hamel and Prahalad
Drucker
Autocratic leaders are dictators who break the law.
Economies of scale means total costs decrease as the business grows.
Economies of scale means a business saves the economy money.
Cost advantages a firm gains as it grows — average cost per unit falls because fixed costs spread over more units, bulk discounts, and specialisation become possible.

mcqs.q: How does HRM differ from traditional personnel management?
options: HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
HRM and personnel are exactly the same thing — just a name change.
Economies of scale means a business saves the economy money.
HRM treats people as a strategic asset and integrates human resource policies with business strategy; personnel management is more administrative and reactive, handling hiring, pay and disputes.

mcqs.q: When might an autocratic leadership style be appropriate?
options: Autocratic leaders are dictators who break the law.
HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
In crises requiring quick decisions, when workers are inexperienced, or in highly hierarchical contexts — though it can damage morale long-term.
Autocratic leadership is always wrong and democratic leadership is always right.
